one_month_reasoning: The company has not yet announced its Q1 FY27 date; past fiscal Q1 releases came Nov 2-7 (supervisor's EDGAR check), so the print almost surely falls after the window. Nov 1, 2026 is a Sunday, so the effective mark is the Oct 30 close. Events inside the window: the hyperscaler September-quarter reports in late October (MSFT/GOOGL/META ~Oct 27-29, AMZN ~Oct 29-30), where 2027 capex commentary is the main read-through for optics. Consensus already sits near $1T for 2027 capex [15], so the bar is high. Sector headline risk is two-way: the Sep 28 selloff on a bullish Citi $11B-by-2030 OCS call reversed within a day [24]. The stock is up ~20% in a week to a 52-week high [16][17], so short-term reversal roughly offsets momentum. I keep the distribution symmetric in log terms around ~$1,080 (just below spot) with a monthly sigma of ~25%, close to the brief's 97%/3.5 = 28% rule, trimmed because the realized vol includes the re-rating.

thesis_break_reason: $600 is ~17x FY28 consensus EPS of ~$34.7 [21], below the bottom of the peer forward P/E range (20.5-62.4x) on earnings a year further out. At that level the market would have stopped believing FY28 numbers: a 2027 hyperscaler capex cut, loss of Nvidia CPO/laser position, or a fast EML price collapse as industry capacity doubles. At 97% realized vol, $750-850 is reachable on ordinary volatility without breaking the thesis.

reasoning: Company facts: Q4 FY26 revenue $1.01B (+109% y/y), non-GAAP GM 50.4%, EPS $3.23; Q1 FY27 guide $1.25B / $4.20 [1]. Current consensus is FY27 ~$20-22 and FY28 ~$33-35 (StockAnalysis $21.78/$34.73 [21]; supervisor's MarketBeat check $19.78/$32.96). The CEO's ~$40 is a verbal earnings-power remark, which I now treat as an upper anchor, not guidance [20]. At $1,085 the stock trades at ~50x FY27 and ~31x FY28 consensus. Industry lane: the chain confirms demand through at least mid-2027: Coherent's FY27 book is full and its InP output is up 80% [4][5], Fabrinet DC +68% [6], Ciena guides FY27 +30% [7], InnoLight/Eoptolink +182%/+100% on 1.6T [8][9], hyperscaler capex near $1T in 2027 [15], Nvidia has locked EML capacity with lead times beyond 2027 [23], and Citi sizes OCS at $11B by 2030 [24]. The chain also carries the main risk: EML/CW capacity doubling [11][4], CSPs qualifying second sources and CW+SiPh [23], and LightCounting's 2-3-year boom then flat/down pattern [10]. Valuation, revised after the supervisor: NTM EPS at the horizon cut from $38 to $36 (consensus-anchored); forward multiple raised from 30x to 32x and checked against 12 listed peers (NTM P/E median 38.3x, next-FY median 29.1x); the cycle leg now haircuts EPS only and uses a normal 30x instead of 28x, removing the double count; net cash (~$10.7/sh) added. Fair value ~$1,045 (from $985), ~4% below spot. Scenarios bear $520/25%, base $1,165/45%, bull $1,900/30% (mean ~$1,225). Ladder: a lognormal with median ~$1,070 and sigma ~0.68, slightly fattened left tail for a cycle turn, giving P(>= $1,085) = 0.49. Research this round: 2 web searches, 2 page fetches, and StockAnalysis statistics/forecast pages for LITE and 12 peers; the Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage fundamentals endpoints were unavailable (plan limit / rate limit).

comps_summary.lite_today: Forward P/E 49.84x on FY27 consensus $21.78 [21][22], ~31x FY28 $34.73; NTM EV/EBITDA ~38x on my non-GAAP estimate (EV ~$110.7B at 103M diluted shares less $1.1B net cash; EBITDA proxied by op income at ~40% margin on $6.34B FY27 / $9.68B FY28 consensus revenue [1][21]), so LITE is at a premium today on both measures
comps_summary.lite_in_my_methods: Forward leg 32x and cycle leg 30x: both inside the peer forward range, 16-22% below the 38.3x NTM median and at or just above the 29.1x next-fiscal-year median. The implied EV/EBITDA at my fair value (~$106B EV on ~$4.1B Oct-2027 NTM EBITDA) is ~26x, just above the 23.5x peer median and inside the range.
comps_summary.justification: I hold LITE at a discount to the peer NTM median, not a premium, for reasons I expect to persist through Oct 2027 rather than for any sector-outperformance view. (1) Growth is not an edge: LITE's next-year EPS growth (59.5% [21]) is in line with the peer median (~57%), so it does not earn a growth premium. (2) Returns on capital are below median: LITE's ROIC is 16.0% [22] against a peer median of ~24%. (3) Earnings quality and cyclicality: LITE's ~40% operating margin rests on scarcity pricing for 200G EMLs [1][14] while industry EML/InP capacity roughly doubles [4][11] and buyers qualify second sources and CW+SiPh [23]. Its own history shows the cycle: revenue fell 23% in FY24 [21], and component makers carry more cyclicality than the systems and diversified peers (ANET, GLW, AVGO). (4) Concentration: two customers were ~42% of FY26 revenue (10-K, per supervisor). (5) Balance sheet is a modest plus (~$1.1B net cash vs net debt at COHR, CIEN, MRVL, AVGO, GLW [22] and peer pages) but too small (~1% of market cap) to offset the above. Because the multiple is applied to EPS a year out, when growth across the group will have slowed, the right comparison is between the peer NTM median (38.3x) and the peer next-fiscal-year median (29.1x); 32x and 30x sit in that band. The direct optical-component peers (COHR 35.8x, AAOI 50.2x, MTSI 39.0x, FN 25.5x) have a median of ~37x, which is consistent with this.
comps_summary.fewer_than_12_note: 12 peers used; Chinese optical module makers (InnoLight, Eoptolink) are close comparables but were left out because I had no comparable cited consensus multiple for them.
